title: Bigfoot Has Been Leaving Some Pretty Big Footprints
excerpt: Have you or anyone you know thought you saw evidence of Bigfoot?
content:
I don't quite know how to explain my belief system regarding Bigfoot. I've never dismissed the possibility of its existence because scientists discover new species of critters all the time. And there are undoubtedly others that have yet to be discovered because they're so difficult to reach. (I'm thinking of species deep in the ocean or in very dense jungles.) Of course, neither of those would be a typical Bigfoot habitat.

Then there's the other voice that says, "Okay, undiscovered species. Got it. Tell me how something that big can hide for decades, if not centuries." Good point, other voice.

If you've ever wondered whether the federal government has any information about Bigfoot, here's something that might interest you. The U.S. Forest Service has quietly released a collection of historical documents involving reports of the legendary creature, also known as Sasquatch.

And some of the stories are pretty interesting.

The documents were added to the Forest Service's online Freedom of Information Act (FOIA) Reading Room on October 15, 2026. The collection is titled "Bigfoot/Sasquatch Records" and contains three historical accounts involving unusual footprints and possible encounters in Montana and Oregon.

Before anybody starts looking for a government-issued Bigfoot identification card, there's an important distinction. The documents do not confirm the existence of Bigfoot. Instead, they provide a fascinating look at reports that were collected and, in one case, investigated by government employees.

A Missing Elk, Strange Footprints and Something in the Woods

One of the documents comes from a Montana resident named Leo T. Kinney, who wrote about the history of the Petty Creek area.

Kinney described an incident in which he and three other people went into the woods to retrieve an elk carcass. When they arrived, they discovered that only the animal's entrails remained.

What happened to the rest of the elk?

According to Kinney, large footprints led away through the snow. He believed whatever had made them had picked up the animal and carried it away.

The group followed the tracks for approximately half a mile before deciding they weren't particularly interested in finding out what had made them.

A similar incident reportedly happened the following year. Another hunter named W.W. Schmitz encountered unusual tracks in the area, along with a strong odor and a strange grunting sound.

Interestingly, nobody actually saw the creature.

Forest Service Investigated 15-Inch Footprints

Perhaps the most intriguing document involves an actual investigation conducted by the Forest Service in 1982.

Wildlife biologist Rodney Johnson was asked to investigate reports of enormous footprints in the Mill Creek watershed of Oregon's Umatilla National Forest.

Investigators examined tracks at two of the three reported locations, photographed the impressions and made plaster casts of four footprints.

One footprint measured approximately 15 inches long and 7 inches wide.

Johnson wasn't convinced the tracks belonged to a giant, two-legged creature. He noted several inconsistencies, including the fact that the impressions weren't as deep as the investigators' own boot prints and that the stride remained approximately four feet regardless of the slope.

Johnson also noted that the impressions looked very natural. He acknowledged that if someone had fabricated the tracks, they had gone to considerable trouble and attention to detail.

A U.S. Border Patrol agent named Joel Hardin was less impressed. In a subsequent memorandum, he described the tracks as a clever attempt at a hoax.

The investigation included photographs of the footprints, which are among the materials now available to the public.

Montana Newspaper Reported Hundreds of Strange Tracks

The third document is a newspaper clipping from the Valley Press in Montana, published in January.

It describes the discovery of hundreds of unusual footprints near River Road West.

Some of the prints reportedly measured 16½ inches long and 8½ inches wide, with an average stride of approximately five feet.

Several people examined the tracks, and some were convinced they were looking at something unusual. One witness even estimated the creature responsible could have weighed between 800 and 1,000 pounds.

That was an estimate based on the size of the prints, not an actual measurement, of course.

Unfortunately for anyone hoping to follow the trail, rain washed away most of the footprints the following day.

You Can Read the Bigfoot Files Yourself

All three documents are available through the U.S. Forest Service's online FOIA Reading Room, where they're listed under the heading "Bigfoot/Sasquatch Records."

The collection includes the original historical accounts, investigative memoranda, photographs and newspaper coverage.

So, has the federal government finally solved the mystery of Bigfoot?

Not exactly.

But if you're among those who have always been fascinated by the possibility that something enormous might be wandering around in the woods, these newly accessible records make for some pretty interesting reading.

And who knows? Maybe there's more to the story than we realize.

Another Bigfoot Mystery Recently Made Headlines

This isn't the first time Bigfoot has made news around here recently. In October, we told you about a documentary called Capturing Bigfoot, which examines the famous 1967 footage of an unidentified figure walking through a California forest.

The film explores claims that newly discovered footage may show the original filmmakers rehearsing the scene before recording what became the most famous piece of supposed Bigfoot evidence in history.
